summary: WebSocket-controlled remote shell and filesystem access on installer host
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent connects to a configurable WebSocket server (default ws://localhost:3456, overridable via serverUrl / SERVER_URL) and routes inbound messages to handlers that spawn a PTY (bash / powershell / cmd) and pipe remote bytes directly into it, plus handlers that read, write, delete, and move files, run git commit/push, proxy HTTP/WebSocket traffic, and restart or upgrade the agent. Any party that reaches the paired server and holds the shared secret can execute arbitrary commands and read/modify arbitrary files on the host running the agent. On first startup the agent also clones https://github.com/yeaft/yeaft-skills.git into ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/, chmods hook scripts to 0755, enables a plugin entry in ~/.claude/settings.json, and (via the service subcommand) writes a systemd user unit that auto-restarts the agent and adds ~/.local/bin, ~/.npm-global/bin, /usr/local/bin, and /usr/bin to PATH — providing persistence for the remote-shell channel. No malicious code executes at npm install (no lifecycle hooks); the remote-control surface activates when the operator starts the agent CLI.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
